title: PIT 8253/8254 (Programmable Interval Timer)
summary: The PIT 8253/8254 is a 3-channel timer. Channel 0: system timer (IRQ0, 18.2 Hz default). Channel 1: DRAM refresh (legacy). Channel 2: speaker (tone generation). Each channel: 16-bit counter, 4 modes (mode 0: interrupt on terminal count, mode 2: rate generator, mode 3: square wave, mode 4: software triggered strobe). Control word: 0x43 (port 0x43). Counter access: 0x40 (ch0), 0x41 (ch1), 0x42 (ch2).

ext.summary: The PIT 8253/8254 is a 3-channel timer. Channel 0: system timer (IRQ0, 18.2 Hz default). Channel 1: DRAM refresh (legacy). Channel 2: speaker (tone generation). Each channel: 16-bit counter, 4 modes (mode 0: interrupt on terminal count, mode 2: rate generator, mode 3: square wave, mode 4: software triggered strobe). Control word: 0x43 (port 0x43). Counter access: 0x40 (ch0), 0x41 (ch1), 0x42 (ch2).

structure.meaning: Bits 6-7: channel (00=ch0, 01=ch1, 10=ch2, 11=read-back). Bits 4-5: access mode (00=latch, 01=LSB, 10=MSB, 11=LSB then MSB). Bits 1-3: mode (000=mode 0, 010=mode 2, 011=mode 3, 100=mode 4). Bit 0: BCD (0=binary, 1=BCD).
System timer. Default: 1193182 Hz / 65536 = 18.2 Hz. IRQ0.
DRAM refresh (legacy, unused on modern systems).
Speaker. Connected to PC speaker via gate (port 0x61 bit 0/1).
Interrupt on terminal count: counter decrements to 0, then IRQ.
Rate generator: periodic interrupts at counter rate.
Square wave: 50% duty cycle. Used for speaker tone.
Software triggered strobe: one-shot pulse on terminal count.

ext.example_decoded: PIT control word: channel 0, LSB+MSB, mode 3 (square wave), binary
notes: Default timer: 65536 ticks = 18.2 Hz (system tick for Linux/Windows).
PIT is legacy (replaced by HPET and TSC).
Mode 3 (square wave) is used for generating tones (e.g., BIOS beep).
